title: How Many Stars?
body:
Goal: ask how many stars to draw (1 to 10), then draw a row of them. Use if / elif / else and comparisons (> and <) to keep the answer sensible.

  1. Open starter.py and press Run (F5). Type 3. Three stars!
  2. Now try 25. The stars run off the screen! Try 0. Nothing at all.
  3. Follow the # TODO: before drawing,
    • if stars > 10: print a message and set stars = 10,
    • elif stars < 1: print a message and set stars = 1,
    • else: print "Coming right up!".
  4. Test with 3, 25 and 0.

Done looks like: 25 becomes 10 stars, 0 becomes 1 star, and the program always tells you what it is doing.

Extra: ask a second question, "Big or small stars?", and use the answer to choose the star size (50 or 25).

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Find the three # TODO lines in starter.py. They sit right after the line that turns the answer into a number. Think about three cases: too many stars, too few, and just right.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Use if, elif and else so Python picks exactly one case. Compare stars with a number using > (bigger than) or < (smaller than). Inside each case, print a message. For the first two, also change stars to a safe number.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: The first case is if stars > ____:. The second is elif stars < ____:. Under each one, use print(...) and then stars = ____ to set a safe number. The last case is just else: with a print. Remember the colons.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# How Many Stars?
# Ask a number, check it is sensible, then draw that many stars.

import turtle

t = turtle.Turtle()
t.speed(0)
t.pensize(2)
t.color("#000000", "#F0E442")   # black outline, yellow inside

answer = input("How many stars? (1 to 10) ")
stars = int(answer)

# TODO: if stars > 10: print a message and set stars = 10
# TODO: elif stars < 1: print a message and set stars = 1
# TODO: else: print("Coming right up!")

# Draw a row of stars, starting on the left
t.penup()
t.goto(-300, 0)
for i in range(stars):
    t.pendown()
    t.begin_fill()
    for point in range(5):
        t.forward(50)
        t.right(144)
    t.end_fill()
    t.penup()
    t.forward(60)       # move along to the next star

turtle.done()
